# .Vary adds names to the Vary response header instead of replacing it, so a
# page and a partial it calls can each name the request headers they read.
# .Header "Vary" would keep only the last value. A name already present is not
# added twice, whatever its case.

muxt generate
grep 'func.*\) Vary\(' template_routes.go

muxt check
exec go test -v

-- go.mod --
module example.com

go 1.25
-- in.go --
package main

func main() {}
-- template.go --
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed template.gohtml
var templatesDir embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesDir, "template.gohtml"))
-- template.gohtml --
{{define "GET / 200"}}{{.Vary "HX-Request"}}{{template "partial" .}}<main>page</main>{{end}}
{{define "partial"}}{{.Vary "HX-Target" "hx-request"}}<p>partial</p>{{end}}
-- template_test.go --
package main

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"slices"
	"testing"
)

func TestVary(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, nil)

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil))

	got := slices.Clone(rec.Header().Values("Vary"))
	slices.Sort(got)
	if want := []string{"HX-Request", "HX-Target"}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("Vary = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
